practices.practice: Create one MongoClient / AsyncMongoClient per process and reuse it (singleton) rather than creating a new client per request, and cache it across warm serverless invocations.
practices.prior_belief: Create and reuse a single Motor/MongoClient instance for the whole process (singleton) and configure connection pooling (e.g., maxPoolSize=100) rather than creating a client per request.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB MongoDB driver connection pooling Motor MongoClient best practices

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS (e.g., include tls=true in the connection string) and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB MongoDB driver connection pooling Motor MongoClient best practices

practices.practice: Do not store DOCUMENTDB_URI or credentials in source control or logs; load credentials from environment variables or retrieve them at runtime from Key Vault or use Microsoft Entra/managed identity.
practices.prior_belief: Respect Azure secrets best practices: do not store DOCUMENTDB_URI or keys in source or logs; load the connection string from environment variables or retrieve it at runtime from Azure Key Vault or another secret store.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB MongoDB driver connection pooling Motor MongoClient best practices

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) + RBAC / managed identities for app authentication rather than long-lived DB passwords; create least-privilege secondary users if SCRAM is necessary.
practices.source_name: documentdb-security
practices.how_found: documentdb-security

practices.practice: Create explicit indexes that match your query patterns, and add a compound index for common group-by queries (e.g., message_type + value_date) rather than relying on many single-field indexes.
practices.source_name: Manage indexing in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB indexing best practices; Manage indexing in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

practices.practice: Design compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) so filters and sorts are served by the index, and prefer a single well-designed compound index over many overlapping single-field indexes.
practices.source_name: documentdb-indexing
practices.how_found: documentdb-indexing

practices.practice: Run explain()/explain('executionStats') on queries and aggregation pipelines to verify index usage and to tune pipelines (apply match/project before group/sort where possible).
practices.source_name: Migrate to ordered indexes in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB explain() and index migration guidance

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation and RU consumption so you can detect and act on throttling and slow queries.
practices.source_name: documentdb-monitoring
practices.how_found: documentdb-monitoring

practices.practice: Respect backpressure: when the service returns HTTP 429 use the Retry-After header if present and otherwise apply exponential backoff with jitter; enqueue retries rather than blocking threads and limit retry counts.
practices.prior_belief: Respect and implement Azure Cosmos/Mongo API rate limiting: on HTTP 429 responses read the Retry-After header and implement exponential backoff with jitter before retrying.
practices.source_name: Design throttling to improve resilience
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB 429 Retry-After header retry backoff

practices.practice: For high-throughput ingestion use bulk/unordered writes (e.g., insertMany / bulk_write with ordered=false) and tune batch sizes (commonly up to ~1,000 documents per batch per process) and concurrency to maximize throughput while watching throttling.
practices.prior_belief: Use bulk unordered writes for ingestion (ordered=False / bulk_write with ordered=False or insert_many with ordered=False) and batch documents in sizes like 100–1000 to maximize throughput and avoid single-request timeouts.
practices.source_name: Optimize write performance in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB bulk write throughput best practices

practices.practice: Plan document sizes for the 16 MB BSON limit (enable 16-MB document support where required) and keep documents well under the limit; store large payloads externally and reference them if needed.
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Document size and batch write limits Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Store monetary amounts using a fixed-point representation or Decimal128 (BSON Decimal128) rather than binary float to avoid precision errors when summing in aggregation pipelines.
practices.prior_belief: If storing numeric amounts, store them as fixed-point (integer cents) or Decimal128 rather than float to avoid precision errors when summing totals in aggregation pipelines.
practices.source_name: Supported features and syntax in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB 7.0 server version
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Decimal128 support

practices.practice: For time-series/daily aggregations keep a date-truncated field (or use $dateTrunc/$dateToString in pipelines) so daily grouping is efficient and indexable rather than scanning full timestamps.
practices.prior_belief: For time-series/aggregation workloads, store both the full ISO timestamp (message_date) and a truncated date field (e.g., message_date_day as YYYY-MM-DD) you can group on — this makes daily aggregation efficient and indexable.
practices.source_name: $dateTrunc
practices.how_found: $dateTrunc date truncation operator

practices.practice: Choose a partition key with high cardinality and even distribution to avoid hot partitions and to make writes and aggregations scale, and design queries to target partition keys when possible.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a partition key with high cardinality and even distribution (e.g., a hashed sender/sender_bic or a synthetic bucketed_date + sender) when creating the collection so writes and aggregations do not create hot partitions.
practices.source_name: Design a data partitioning strategy
practices.how_found: Design partitioning strategy Azure Cosmos DB

practices.practice: Configure per-operation timeouts and server-selection / socket timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS) appropriate to your environment to avoid indefinite hangs and detect connectivity problems quickly.
practices.prior_belief: Implement per-operation timeouts and serverSelectionTimeoutMS/ socketTimeoutMS on the client to avoid indefinite hangs (e.g., serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, socketTimeoutMS appropriate for bulk ops).
practices.source_name: documentdb-connection
practices.how_found: documentdb-connection

practices.practice: Azure's MongoDB-compatible service ignores client-specified MongoDB writeConcern (w/wtimeout); rely on account consistency settings and the platform's replication semantics rather than setting client writeConcern to tune durability.
practices.prior_belief: Use ordered=False and writeConcern w/ appropriate w and wtimeout only if you understand tradeoffs; for maximum throughput prefer lower synchronous write guarantees but ensure app-level validation/compensation for data loss.
practices.source_name: Supported features and syntax in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB 4.0 server version
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB writeConcern mapping and behavior

practices.practice: Enforce idempotency by recording a unique message identifier and using unique indexes / upserts to avoid duplicate ingestion, but create unique indexes carefully (unique indexes on sharded collections must include the shard key and unique indexes on existing non-empty collections may be restricted).
practices.prior_belief: Keep parsers and validation idempotent: include a unique message_id and use upsert with a unique index on message_id to avoid duplicate ingestion from retries.
practices.source_name: Manage indexing in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB unique index guidance

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes (collection-level _ts or custom TTL field) or scheduled archival to expire or move old documents rather than retaining all documents in the hot collection indefinitely.
practices.source_name: Supported features and syntax in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB 5.0 server version
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB TTL and custom TTL guidance

practices.practice: For vector search, store embeddings in a dedicated field and create a platform-specific cosmosSearch vector index, choosing DiskANN/HNSW/IVF by scale and normalizing embeddings when using cosine similarity.
practices.source_name: documentdb-vector-search
practices.how_found: documentdb-vector-search

practices.practice: Test aggregation and index changes in staging with real or seeded data and use explain/MCP tools to verify indexes and plans before promoting to production.
practices.prior_belief: Seed test data and run aggregation queries in a staging environment first; use the documentdb MCP/explain tools to verify created indexes and query plans rather than relying on assumptions.
practices.source_name: Use Beanie with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Python inventory API
practices.how_found: Beanie + Azure DocumentDB tutorial; mention of testing and validation

practices.practice: Do not commit .env files with secrets; commit a .env.example with placeholders and instruct operators to load credentials from Key Vault or environment injection.
practices.prior_belief: Do not commit .env files containing secrets; commit a .env.example with placeholders and instruct operators to populate real credentials from Key Vault or environment injection.
practices.source_name: .env.example / README.md
practices.how_found: .env.example and README in repository

practices.practice: Ensure TLS validation is enabled by default and validate server certificates; do not disable TLS in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL for connections and validate server certificates when possible (use the driver default TLS mode) to protect credentials and PII in transit.
practices.source_name: documentdb-security
practices.how_found: documentdb-security

practices.practice: Instrument the ingest pipeline with tracing and metrics (requests/sec, errors, avg latency, bulk insert sizes, RU consumption, 429 counts) and alert on anomaly thresholds so production issues can be triaged quickly.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument request/ingest pipeline with tracing and metrics (requests/sec, errors, avg latency, bulk insert sizes, RU consumption, 429 counts) so production issues can be triaged quickly.
